title: They Took Gas Out of the Inflation Number
summary: Bitcoin-channel take on the September 2026 CPI: headline 3.7 is the real number, core 2.6 hides the gas and heating-oil surge, inflation is accelerating, and only Bitcoin's fixed supply escapes the money printer.

assertions.quote: That is core inflation. It is inflation with the parts that hurt taken out.

verdicts.note: Core inflation forecasts future headline inflation better than headline does, which is why the Fed watches it, but it understates the cost of living when energy stays high.

assertions.quote: That one item caused more than half of the whole month's increase.

verdicts.note: Gasoline rose about 9 percent in September 2026 and accounted for more than half of the 0.6 percent monthly CPI rise, per the BLS release.

assertions.quote: Prices sped up four months in a row.

verdicts.note: Monthly CPI went from -0.4 in June to 0.1, 0.4 and 0.6 percent through September 2026, and the annual rate rose from 3.4 to 3.7.
Seasonally adjusted monthly all-items CPI changes ran -0.4% (June), 0.1% (July), 0.4% (August), 0.6% (September 2026): three consecutive months of acceleration.

assertions.quote: Groceries actually dipped a little in September.

verdicts.note: Food at home fell 0.1 percent in September 2026 and is up under 2 percent on the year, while energy rose 5.2 percent in the month.

assertions.quote: When the government needs more of them, it makes more of them. That is where inflation comes from in the first place.

verdicts.note: Sustained inflation needs monetary accommodation, but the 2021-2022 and 2026 episodes were driven largely by supply shocks in goods and energy, and money growth tracks prices poorly at short horizons.

assertions.quote: To find something the printer cannot reach.

verdicts.note: The supply cap is real, but Bitcoin fell about 65 percent in 2022 while CPI peaked and trades like a risk asset, so it has not protected purchasing power over inflationary stretches.
